doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

chapter: Growing up with his father and Joe Morello
title: Father the keyboardist who tried to keep him out of music
summary: Born 1950, he grew up with jazz records; his legally blind father tried to steer him away from music, but he took up drums.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well we coincidentally just found out that we were both born in 1950. And it was an okay year to be born I guess. What do you remember, as a child, the first kind of music from either records or radio that kind of seeped into your consciousness?

Before I was born my father was a professional musician. And he was friends with Phil Woods, the famous jazz saxophone player, Sal Salvador, a great jazz guitarist, and Joe Morello, a phenomenal drummer. And he used to always be playing their records or the records of the jazz masters all the time. So I had to be exposed to it before I was born. So I feel that that was a big influence.
Yeah your fate was kind of cast early, wasn’t it?
So there definitely was jazz in your house.
Did you — what did your father play?
My father was a keyboard player.
Did he give you instruction or tips?

Actually he tried to keep me out of the business. As we know it’s not an easy profession, it can be pretty brutal, and he didn’t want me exposed to that, so he tried to keep me out of it. And it didn’t work of course, I didn’t listen. My father was legally blind and my mom had to drive him to all of the jobs, so I got to hear like the first couple tunes and the last couple tunes, and I really took an interest in the drums, because he played a lot of Joe Morello’s albums and I was just drawn to the drums. And eventually I was able to borrow a pair of sticks from the drummer and started to teach myself a little bit.
And your father’s going no, no.
What did he envision for you? Did you have other talents that he thought that you could pursue? Or interests?
I had math aptitude to I guess banker, insurance, salesman, something like that. But he just didn’t want me in the music field.
